title: Closed tensor structure and internal-Hom finiteness for adic constructible complexes
statement:
Let $k$ be any field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ use the completed ring sheaf $\widehat R_T=\varprojlim_n(R/\varpi^n)_T$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and the integral category $\mathcal I_T=D^b_c(T,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Use completed tensor $\widehat\otimes_R^L$ and ambient derived internal Hom $H_R$ [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

For $P,Q\in\mathcal I_T$, the object $H_R(P,Q)$ belongs to $\mathcal I_T$. With these operations $\mathcal I_T$ is closed symmetric monoidal: for $M,P,Q\in\mathcal I_T$ tensor evaluation induces a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}(M\widehat\otimes_R^LP,Q)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,H_R(P,Q)).$$
The tensor unit is $\widehat R_T$. These are the evaluation and adjunction of the ambient ringed-site internal Hom restricted to complete constructible objects, using completed tensor. In particular the integral category here is a category of modules over $\widehat R_T$, not over the discrete constant sheaf $R$.

Let $E\subset L$ be a finite extension with $S=\mathcal O_L$, and let $P\mapsto P\otimes_RS$ be integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. For $P,Q\in\mathcal I_T$ the evaluation-defined comparison $H_R(P,Q)\otimes_RS\to H_S(P\otimes_RS,Q\otimes_RS)$, the transpose of the scalar extension of evaluation $H_R(P,Q)\widehat\otimes_R^LP\to Q$ composed with the tensor comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], is an isomorphism, natural in $P$ and $Q$. It is the identity for $L=E$ and, for $E\subset L\subset L'$, is compatible with the composition isomorphisms of scalar extension. Consequently scalar extension carries evaluation and the tensor–Hom adjunction bijections over $R$ to those over $S$.

source.place: Lemmas 6.7.12 and 6.7.13 (finite type over a field is quasi-excellent), with completed tensor–Hom adjunction in the derived-complete category, Sections 6.5 and 6.7

proof.text: Put $t=\varpi$, $B=\widehat R_T$ and $B_n=(R/t^n)_T$. The coefficient ring $R$ is a Noetherian DVR with finite residue field by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], $B$ is flat over the constant $R$-sheaf and $B/t^nB=B_n$. Thus $t$ acts injectively on $B$: tensor the injection $R\xrightarrow{t}R$ with the flat sheaf $B$. The scheme $T$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] (every ideal of a field is zero or the unit ideal) and finite-dimensional by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. The one-stratum perfect model $R[0]$ gives $B\in\mathcal I_T$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. In particular the proposed tensor unit is an actual complete constructible object.

source.place: Definition 6.5.1, Proposition 6.6.11; coefficient sheaf and uniform reduction conventions

proof.text:
Let $C$ denote the completion reflector of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector] for the ringed site $(T_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$ and the single generator $t$. Its universal property is $\operatorname{Hom}(CV,Q)=\operatorname{Hom}(V,Q)$ when $Q$ is complete. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], its Koszul model is canonically $R\varprojlim_n(V\otimes_B^LB_n)$, with the same unit. For K-flat representatives $F,G$ of $M,P$, termwise associativity and balancing give
$$(F\otimes_BG)\otimes_BB_n\cong(F\otimes_BB_n)\otimes_{B_n}(G\otimes_BB_n),\quad (f\otimes g)\otimes a\mapsto(f\otimes1)\otimes(g\otimes a).$$
The inverse multiplies the two coefficients. These maps commute with the total differential and all quotient transitions. Therefore the tower defining completed tensor in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] is exactly the reduction tower of $M\otimes_B^LP$, and $M\widehat\otimes_R^LP=C(M\otimes_B^LP)$ compatibly with the completion unit. This verifies the comparison, rather than treating it as part of the definition.

source.place: Sections 3.4–3.5, Definition 3.4.10; comparison with the explicit strict reduction tower

proof.text:
For $P,Q\in\mathcal I_T$ put $H=H_R(P,Q)$. Since $Q$ is complete, [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction] proves that $H$ is complete and gives the evaluation-defined isomorphisms
$$H\otimes_B^LB_n\cong R\mathcal Hom_{B_n}(P\otimes_B^LB_n,Q\otimes_B^LB_n).$$
Write $P_1=P\otimes_B^LB_1$, $Q_1=Q\otimes_B^LB_1$. These are bounded constructible by the definition of $\mathcal I_T$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. The ring $A_1=R/t$ is a finite field by the DVR assertion in [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]. A bounded complex of sheaves of vector spaces has finite Tor amplitude: tensoring with a degree-zero vector-space sheaf is exact, and so does not enlarge its cohomological interval. Equivalently this is checked on the etale-origin complexes here, where every vector-space stalk is flat, and pulled back to the pro-etale site. Thus $P_1,Q_1$ satisfy the finite-Tor hypotheses.

source.place: Lemma 3.4.11 and the reduction comparison of Lemma 6.7.13

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-finite-tor-internal-hom-any-field] to $X=T$, the given field $k$, and $n=1$, with $K=P_1$ and $M=Q_1$. All its coefficient, invertibility, finite-type and separatedness hypotheses are among the hypotheses of this item. Its conclusion and Step 3 give $H_1=H\otimes_B^LB_1\in D^b_c(T,A_1)$. Choose integers $a\leq b$ containing its cohomology, taking $a=b=0$ if $H_1=0$. Only the residue coefficient field is used in this finiteness invocation; no assertion of a uniform bound over different coefficient rings is borrowed from that lemma.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.13 at the residue coefficient field

proof.text:
Set $H_n=H\otimes_B^LB_n$. For each $n>1$ the sequence
$$0\longrightarrow A_1\xrightarrow{\bar x\mapsto t^{n-1}x}A_n\longrightarrow A_{n-1}\longrightarrow0$$
is exact by cancellation in the DVR. Its constant sheaves, viewed as $B$-modules, give a distinguished triangle by [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle]. Tensoring a flat-term K-flat representative of $H$ keeps it short exact. Hence there is a triangle $H_1\to H_n\to H_{n-1}\to H_1[1]$, also in $A_n$-modules via the quotient coefficient actions. Induct on $n$. The base is Step 4. For the induction step, [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] shows vanishing outside the SAME $[a,b]$. For each degree its middle cohomology is an extension of a cokernel involving $H^{q-1}(H_{n-1})$ and $H^q(H_1)$ by a kernel involving $H^q(H_{n-1})$ and $H^{q+1}(H_1)$. The weak Serre property [lem-sfb-discrete-noetherian-constructible-serre] makes these constructible in its affine-local sense; an $A_j$-sheaf viewed along $A_n\twoheadrightarrow A_j$ keeps its finite locally constant models. On the Noetherian $T$ of Step 1 this sense agrees with the global partitions of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] (finite and finitely presented $A_n$-modules coincide): intersect a global partition with an affine open $U$, locally closed subsets of a Noetherian space being constructible; conversely, for a finite affine cover $U_1,\dots,U_m$ with partitions $Z_{i,a}$ of $U_i$, the reduced strata $Z_{i,a}\setminus(U_1\cup\dots\cup U_{i-1})$ partition $T$, and inverse image along their immersions into $Z_{i,a}$ keeps local constancy and stalks. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin] each $H_n$ has bounded constructible etale origin. Together with completeness from Step 3 and the uniform interval just proved, [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] gives $H\in\mathcal I_T$.

source.place: Definition 6.5.1 and Lemma 6.5.3; explicit uniform-bound induction from the residue field

proof.text:
The completed tensor of two objects of $\mathcal I_T$ belongs to $\mathcal I_T$ by [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible]. For $M,P,Q\in\mathcal I_T$, Step 2 and the reflector property give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(M\widehat\otimes_R^LP,Q)=\operatorname{Hom}(M\otimes_B^LP,Q).$$
The ringed-site currying isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], followed by $H^0$ global sections as in [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections], identifies the latter group with $\operatorname{Hom}(M,H_R(P,Q))$. Since the subcategory is full and Step 5 places the Hom object in it, these are the required Hom groups in $\mathcal I_T$. All maps are natural; uncurrying sends $u:M\to H_R(P,Q)$ to evaluation composed with $u\otimes1_P$, factored uniquely through completion. Thus the bijection and evaluation are those of the ambient ringed-site adjunction, with completed tensor.

The ordinary tensor symmetry induces the completed symmetry, and $C(B\otimes_B^LM)\cong CM\cong M$ gives the unit constraints. Here is also an explicit way to remove completion from intermediate bracketings. For a complete test object $Q$ and arbitrary $A,D$, [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction] makes $H_R(D,Q)$ complete; currying and the reflector property identify
$$\operatorname{Hom}(C(CA\otimes_B^LD),Q)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(CA,H_R(D,Q))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A,H_R(D,Q))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(C(A\otimes_B^LD),Q).$$
Consequently completing the map $A\otimes D\to CA\otimes D$ is invertible. Apply this to $A=M\otimes P$ (and use symmetry for the other factor): both bracketings of a triple completed tensor identify canonically with $C(M\otimes P\otimes Q)$. This defines the associator. Pentagon, triangle and symmetry identities reduce, by the same bijections, to the corresponding total-tensor identities before completion; those identities are the usual rebracketing, unit multiplication and signed permutation of pure tensors. Thus their two sides are equal and remain equal after completion. With the unit from Step 1 and closure from Step 6 this gives the closed symmetric monoidal structure asserted.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10 and Lemma 3.4.11; universal-property verification of tensor constraints

proof.text:
Let $S=\mathcal O_L$, $B'=\widehat S_T$, and $T_{L/E}$ denote integral scalar extension. By [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], $B'$ is finite free over $B$, and on EVERY complete input $V$ its ordinary extension $V\otimes_B^LB'$ identifies canonically with $T_{L/E}V$. This applies to $P,Q,H_R(P,Q)$ by Steps 3–5. The evaluation-transposed isomorphism of [lem-sf-ringed-finite-free-hom-base-change] therefore gives
$$T_{L/E}H_R(P,Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_S(T_{L/E}P,T_{L/E}Q).$$
Scalar extension preserves $\mathcal I_T$ by [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible]. To check the specified normalization, the ordinary tensor comparison on K-flat representatives sends $(x\otimes s)\otimes(y\otimes t)$ to $(x\otimes y)\otimes st$. Taking its reductions and their limit gives exactly the completed tensor comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], through the tower identifications of Step 2. Precomposing the completed evaluation with its completion unit recovers ordinary evaluation; the finite-free comparison is its transpose by its cited statement. Uniqueness in the completion and tensor-Hom adjunctions therefore identifies the displayed map with the comparison specified in the item. This uses no choice of a finite free basis to define the map.

source.place: Ringed finite-free change of rings: tensor–Hom adjunction, Tags 08J9/08JA; Bhatt–Scholze completed tensor, Definition 3.4.10

proof.text:
The comparison is natural by [lem-sf-ringed-finite-free-hom-base-change] and the natural completion comparison. For $E\subset L\subset L'$ put $B''=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L',T}$. Identify two successive scalar extensions with direct extension using the composition isomorphisms in [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. Uncurry the two candidate Hom comparisons into $Q\otimes_B^LB''$. On simultaneous representatives both evaluate
$$(h\otimes s\otimes s',\ p\otimes u')\longmapsto h(p)\otimes ss'u'.$$
This identity holds in each degree, with the same Hom-complex differential and tensor signs on either route; coefficients have degree zero. Multiplication is associative, so balancing, quotient transitions and completion preserve this equality. The two uncurried maps are equal, hence their transposes are equal by Step 6. For the identity extension the formula is $(h,p)\mapsto h(p)$; the completion unit is the canonical identification of the scalar-extension functor with the identity. Finally, for any $u:M\to H_R(P,Q)$, both 'extend its uncurrying' and 'uncurry the extended $u$ followed by the comparison' send $(m\otimes s,p\otimes t)$ to $\operatorname{ev}(u(m),p)\otimes st$. Thus scalar extension intertwines evaluation and every tensor-Hom adjunction bijection, as well as the identity and tower comparisons.

source.place: Tensor universal maps and evaluation: Tags 08J9/08JA; explicit identity/tower calculation
